subject.title: [Bug]: OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM disable semantics unclear; LaunchAgent still appends after unset/0

question: Should `OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM=0` or an explicit launchd/process-level unset/disable have hard-disable precedence over durable service env/config sources for raw-stream logging?
rationale: Raw-stream logs can contain sensitive prompts and tool output, so the fix depends on maintainer intent for the trust order between launchctl/process env, generated LaunchAgent env files, state-dir `.env`, and config `env`.

options.title: Hard-disable wins
options.body: Treat explicit disabled values such as `0`, `false`, `off`, or an operator disable marker as authoritative over durable raw-stream enablement, then document and test the security-first precedence.

options.title: Durable source wins with warnings
options.body: Keep durable `.env`/config service env as the source of truth but add clear docs, status, and doctor warnings telling operators to remove the persisted raw-stream entry to disable logging.

options.title: Docs-only clarification
options.body: Document the current behavior without changing precedence, accepting that `launchctl unsetenv` or `0` alone may not disable a wrapper-sourced raw-stream env value.

recommendation.title: Hard-disable wins
recommendation.body: Treat explicit disabled values such as `0`, `false`, `off`, or an operator disable marker as authoritative over durable raw-stream enablement, then document and test the security-first precedence.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses raw-stream diagnostics, durable service env, security defaults, and docs, and steipete appears in the relevant raw-stream and service-env history.
